Cortical neuropeptides. Cortical neurons express a number of neuropeptides(Somogyi and   408    Klausberger, 2005), whereby CCK is the most abundant of all. CCK comes in different forms, 409 but it is the sulphated octapeptide, CCK-8S, that predominates in the brain(Dockray et al., 1978;   410    Rehfeld, 1978). CCK is expressed in GABAergic interneurons(Houser et al., 1983), and many411 pyramidal neurons (DeFelipe and Fariñas, 1992) have also high levels of CCK transcript 412 (Burgunder and Young, 1988; Schiffmann and Vanderhaeghen, 1991). The CCK + interneurons 413 are relatively few, but exert a critical control of cortical activity (Somogyi and Klausberger, 414 2005). However, it is CCK in the pyramidal neurons that are in focus in the present study, 415especially the CCK + , glutamatergic projection from EC to AC. We also use exogenous CCK in 416 the experiments, both CCK-8S and CCK-4 which is the C-terminus not only of proCCK but also 417 of gastrin. The small size of the latter fragment is the reason, why it is considered to pass the 418 blood-brain-barrier(Rehfeld, 2000). If we would have increased the number 455 of pairing trials, the effective Delay 1 might have lengthened. 456 Hebbian plasticity. We addressed the issue of spike timing-dependent plasticity and the critical 457 time limit. Here the Hebbian rule has, arguably, been the most influential theory in learning and 458 memory. This rule says that in order to induce potentiation the presynaptic subthreshold input 459 should occur at most 20 ms before post-synaptic firing (Bi and Poo, 1998; Markram et al., 1997; 460 Zhang et al., 1998). However, this theory has been challenged (Drew and Abbott, 2006; 461 Izhikevich, 2007), with a prevalent question being: how can associations be established across 462 behavioral time scales of seconds or even longer if the critical window is only 20 ms? (Bittner et 463 al., 2017). Bittner et al. reported that five pairings of pre-synaptic subthreshold inputs with post-464 synaptic calcium plateau potentials produce a large potentiation; and that presynaptic inputs can 465 arrive seconds before or after postsynaptic activity, a phenomenon termed "behavioral time scale 466 synaptic plasticity" (Bittner et al., 2017). 467 This may account for the highly plastic nature of place fields in the hippocampus. In 468 agreement, we observed potentiation in the neocortex, even when presynaptic input arrived 200 469 ms (Delay 2) earlier than postsynaptic firing and after only five trials pairing, but only in the 470 presence of CCK. This time window could perhaps be extended as the paring trials increase. In 471 general terms, these results fit with the fact that neuropeptides are known to exert slow and long-472lasting effects (van den Pol, 2012). We did not explore the reverse direction, in which post-473 synaptic activity occurred before pre-synaptic activity, because noise stimuli induced more than 474 one spike and thus timing would be difficult to control.
